messages.author: 89c9fc822e34b78c
messages.subject: random crashes under windows: fixed
parts:
Hi all,
Cc: Lisa, Oscar

Both Lisa and Oscar have reported 'random' crashes of lavaan; see:

https://groups.google.com/forum/#!topic/lavaan/8ncLFuKYzuE
https://groups.google.com/forum/#!topic/lavaan/O7GIIqMeIGc

These crashes have haunted me for several weeks now. They only occurred under windows (not linux or mac osx), typically when running a simulation study using categorical data. I was pretty sure that lavaan was innocent (since it is written in R without any compiled code), but I needed to be 100% sure. Perhaps, one of the external packages (e.g. pbivnorm was the culprit. But after a *long* time of testing/debugging, I was able to trace back these crashes to ... the nlminb() function (which is part of the stats package in R). Once I could create a small reproducible script, I filed an official bug report to the R developers (see https://bugs.r-project.org/bugzilla/show_bug.cgi?id=15914). They discovered that the bug was in fact due to an optimization bug in the gcc compiler for windows. But Duncan Murdoch provided a workaround, and this is now fixed in the dev version of R, which you can install from here: http://cran.r-project.org/bin/windows/base/rdevel.html . This version will eventually become R 3.2.0

In the meantime,  if you experience these crashes, you can circumvent the problem by installing the dev version of lavaan (0.5-17.701 or higher) and using control=list(cor.optim.method="BFGS") or control=list(cor.optim.method="optimize"), to change the optimizer needed for computing the polychoric correlations. For the lavPredict() function, we added the argument optim.method, so you can now use lavPredict(fit, optim.method = "BFGS"). But the nlminb() optimizer works (slightly) better (and faster), so installing the dev version of R is perhaps the better solution.

And so, now this is fixed, I can finally sleep well again.

Yves.
